 O R D E R
The revision petitioner herein challenges the conviction and sentence against him under Section 16(1A)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short "the PFA Act").

He faced prosecution in the court below on the allegation that at about 1.00 p.m. on 02.04.1997, when the Food Inspector of the Ettumanoor Circle visited his grocery shop, he was found selling food articles without license under the PFA Act, and some quantity of dal purchased by the Food Inspector for consideration was found adulterated on analysis at the Regional Laboratory.
2.
The prosecution examined five witnesses, and proved Exts.P1 to P20 documents in the trial court.
On a claim of warranty made by the revision petitioner, the second accused was also impleaded during trial.
3. The accused denied the incriminating circumstances when examined under Section 313 Cr.P.C..
In defence, one witness was examined as DW1, and Ext.D1 was also proved.
4. On an appreciation of the evidence, the trial court found the second accused not guilty of any offence, but the first accused was found guilty.

On conviction, he was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for one year, and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/- under Section 16(1A)(i) of the PFA Act,
and for violation of Rule 50 of PFA Rules, that he conducted trade without license, he was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 15 days, and to pay a fine of Rs.500/-.
5.
The accused preferred appeal before the Court of Session against the judgment of conviction dated 19.05.2004, but the appellate court confirmed the conviction and sentence.
Now he is before this Court in revision.

6. When this revision petition came up for hearing, the learned counsel submitted that as regards the conviction under Section 16(1A)(i) of the PFA Act, the recent decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in PEPSICO case is applicable, and the accused will have to be acquitted.
As regards the conviction for violation of Rule 50 of the PFA Rules, the learned counsel pleaded for some leniency in sentence.

7. In Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector (2009 (1) KHC 983), the Honourable Supreme Court has held that in cases where the Central Government has not notified the laboratory for examination of food articles, and also the method of analysis for different items of food articles,
the accused cannot be found guilty.

sentences.text: The present case is such a case where the Government of India has not notified the method of analysis for dal, or the laboratories for analysis.
In view of the decision in Rasheed's case (Supra), I find that PEPSICO decision of the Honourable Supreme Court is applicable, and the accused will have to be acquitted.
8. As regards violation of rule 50 of the PFA Rules, the revision petitioner does not have a case to be argued.
It has come out in evidence that as on the date of detection in this case, he had no license under the PFA Act.
His license had expired on 31.03.1997.
Inspection was made by the Food Inspector on 02.04.1997.
There is nothing to show that he had applied for renewal of license on or before 02.04.1997.
I find that he is liable for conviction for violation of Rule 50 of the PFA Rules.
However, in the present circumstances, I feel it appropriate to modify the sentence.
The trial court has imposed a sentence of simple imprisonment for 15 days, and a fine of Rs.500/- for violation of Rule 50 of the PFA Ruels.
He must be now aged 72 years.
In such a situation, I feel that the minimum possible sentence under the law, and the maximum fine imposed by the trial court will be the adequate sentence.
In the result, the revision petition is allowed in part.
The revision petitioner is found not guilty of the offence under Section 16(1A)(i) of the PFA Act, and he is acquitted of the said offence in revision.
Accordingly the conviction and sentence against him under Section 16(1A)(i) of the PFA Act will stand set aside.
But the conviction for violation of Rule 50 of the PFA Rules is confirmed.

However,
the sentence is modified and reduced to imprisonment till rising of the court.
The fine sentence with the default sentence thereon is maintained.

The petitioner will surrender before the trial court within three weeks from this date to serve out the modified sentence, and to make payment of the fine amount voluntarily, on failure of which steps shall be taken by the trial court to enforce the modified sentence, and realise the amount of fine, or to enforce the default sentence.
